asks.notes: Section B: the "Preparatory work" (scale and chord bank) is MARKED at Ordinary Level ("Grid / Stave", "Up to 2.5 marks per chord", 2.5 x 4 = 10), so its bullets are part of the question text and its line is a counted criterion at the printed 2.5 x 4 (lane ruling: marked preparatory work is counted). JUDGEMENT CALL: the scheme says "Up to" 2.5 a chord, so a part-correct chord may earn less than 2.5, which a counted line on 0/2.5/5/7.5/10 cannot place; the alternative, a no-band criterion, would sit on whole marks 0-10 and could not place 2.5 or 7.5. The chord bank prints I ("The first chord is given") and iii and vii° filled in and shaded, so the four chords asked for are ii, IV, V and vi. The scheme's per-element lines are the criteria: each "1 mark per ... (1 x 12)" line counted, each "Up to 2 marks for quality ... (2 x 4)" line a no-band criterion on 0-8 (the 2022 COVID-adjusted tariff: 10 + 20 + 20 = 50). The Section B general points (scheme p6) are carried on all three questions; "5. ii – 1 generally not accepted" is printed so (sic, for ii – I). The 2022 Ordinary scheme prints NO table of given or accepted chords, so there is no scheme crop. The "1 x 12" / "2 x 4" sit in the scheme's Mark column, not in the descriptor, so the labels carry the descriptor only. Q4's (i)-(iv) name the cadences at A-D; one ask, one total. Key F major, 2/4.

asks.questionText: Adding bass notes and chord indications at cadence points • Write out the scale of D major on the stave below. • Plot the chords available in this key (I, ii, IV, V and vi) either in the chord bank grid or on the stave below. The first chord is given. • Study the piece of music on the following page. • Add suitable bass notes and chord indications to complete the cadences at A, B, C and D. • You may use either chord symbols or Roman numerals, but not both. • Do not repeat the same chord in adjacent boxes.

grid.stem: Answer one question only in this section:
taskRequirements: 1. Same chord in adjacent boxes not accepted
2. Accidental and suffix, where relevant, must be fully correct for mark to be awarded
3. Chords must be part of a good progression
1. No doubling of major 3rd under chord symbol
3. Stepwise movement to and from inversions = good

criteria.label: Up to 2.5 marks per chord
1 mark per correct chord that fits the notes
Up to 2 marks per quality of chord progression at each cadence point, which fits well with the melody
1 mark per correct bass note of the chord and which falls on the correct beat of the bar
Up to 2 marks for quality of bass line at each cadence point, which fits well with the chord progression and melody notes
